assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original transparent raster matte-painting layer for a Godot 2.5D Victorian harbor game, layer 1 of 3: distant waterfront. Create a very wide horizontal panoramic CUTOUT, ideally 3:1 canvas, with the actual painted content a shallow narrow strip across the lower-middle of the canvas and generous fully transparent space above and below it. It must be a game environment layer, not a screenshot or a concept poster. A prosperous sunny nineteenth-century coastal trading city's opposite shoreline: a long irregular crescent of small cream and pale sage stone warehouses, 2–3 floors, slate-brown roofs, timber loading cranes, several distinct projecting piers and tiny distant moored sailing vessels. The city continues beyond the edges but both outer ends taper naturally into lower shore outcrops. Keep the centre shoreline low and allow uneven building clusters and street openings. Individual houses are small relative to the very broad panorama; about 40–60 building fronts, shallow roof height, no giant near building. Existing game's style is deliberately pixel-textured low-poly 3D buildings with warm cream masonry, muted teal trim, brown-grey roofs, crisp simplified shapes, restrained pixel clusters and nearest-neighbor-like edges, with tiny readable architectural detail. Match this illustrated/pixel game language; no photographic finish, no painterly brush smears. View: slight elevated oblique view showing a little roof, nearly level distant shore, coherent one-point distance. Soft clear afternoon light from upper left, warm highlights, cool muted sea-facing shadows. Colors modestly desaturated for distance but no fog or haze. Fully transparent sky AND transparent water: draw only architecture, quay masonry, piers/shore and a few tiny distant boats; the game supplies its own blue sky, clouds and animated sea. Do not paint any sky color, sea area, horizon gradient, white background, checkerboard, text, logo, UI, foreground people, lighthouse, clocktower or framing border. Silhouette edges and openings must have real alpha transparency. Keep any ground plinth narrow and naturally shaped, not a rectangular sheet.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original transparent raster matte-painting layer for a Godot 2.5D Victorian harbor game, layer 2 of 3: dense middle-distance city rooftops. Create a very wide horizontal panoramic CUTOUT, ideally 3:1 canvas, actual painted city forming a shallow uneven narrow strip through the lower-middle with generous fully transparent sky above and transparent space below. It is an environment texture, not a screenshot/poster. A large sunny nineteenth-century merchant city rising gently inland behind its opposite harbor shore. Dense but believable urban blocks with 3–5 storey cream, light sandstone, muted sage and pale dusty rose houses; many varied slate-brown pitched roofs and restrained chimneys. Clear street gaps and small courts break up blocks. Layer many small roofs in depth; increase density and elevation toward the left-centre, taper down toward the right. Uneven crescent skyline; no continuous equal-height wall. About 60–90 small buildings across a very broad panorama; individual floor/roof detail should be small and scale consistent. No giant foreground facade. Style must match a pixel-textured low-poly 3D game: crisp simplified geometric building faces, subtle pixel-cluster texture, warm cream masonry, muted teal trims, brown-grey roofs, restrained edge contrast, detailed enough for a distant background, not photorealistic and not smeared brush painting. Nearly level distant view with slight elevated oblique roof visibility, soft clear afternoon light from upper left, warm highlights and cool low-contrast shadows. A little paler and less contrast than the waterfront layer; no fog, no haze. Draw only the city structures and a narrow natural inland base. Real alpha transparency around the whole silhouette, through street/edge openings, above roofs and below the narrow base. NO sky, no water, no opaque horizon gradient, no checkerboard, no white background, no text, no logos/UI, no foreground people, no lighthouse, no dominant cathedral or clocktower. Those landmarks belong to a separate far layer.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original transparent raster matte-painting layer for a Godot 2.5D Victorian harbor game, layer 3 of 3: far inland hills and landmark skyline. Create a very wide horizontal panoramic CUTOUT, ideally 3:1 canvas, actual painted content a shallow low undulating band through the lower-middle of canvas with generous fully transparent sky above and transparent space below. A far inland skyline of a prosperous nineteenth-century merchant city encircling a harbor: pale blue-green gentle hills, tiny clustered slate-brown rooftops along the slope, ONE recognisable slender clocktower just left of centre marking the civic centre, a smaller muted copper civic dome nearby and one restrained church spire further left. Small chimneys may have tiny discreet wisps, but clear clean sunny sky is supplied by game and must remain transparent. Broad uneven crescent silhouette, denser and a little higher on the left/centre, taper down toward the right with an open lower end. Landmarks should feel distant, small relative to panorama and scaled to ordinary surrounding town roofs, not fantasy skyscrapers or castles. Existing art language is a cozy-bright Victorian port before a dark-fantasy voyage: pixel-textured simplified low-poly geometric buildings, crisp pixel-cluster edges, warm cream stone/cool sage silhouettes, muted slate roofs. Use softer, paler, lower-contrast colors than the foreground town without fog, blur or opaque atmosphere. View almost level from the harbor with very slight elevated roof visibility; same afternoon light upper-left as other layers. Real alpha transparency outside the complete hill/city silhouette and below its narrow uneven base. NO sky paint, no water, no full rectangular mountain base, no white background/checkerboard, no text/logo/UI, no foreground people or ships, no lighthouse (an existing native lighthouse must stay separate). Do not make an equally tall flat wall or oversized central tower.
